Visit note | 2025-03-05 09:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Hafiz Hossain, 27, male. Mr. Hossain visits today complaining of pimples and blackheads on his face, spots on his back, and dark marks left behind after previous pimples healed. He explains that his skin flared up significantly after he started using a heavy face cream bought in Kamrangirchar. He works as a restaurant cook, is exposed to kitchen heat daily, and has no other known skin conditions or medical problems. He denies any fever or joint pain. On examination: about 22 inflamed spots on the face, BP 131/81 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 53 kg. The surrounding skin is oily with several open comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and avoid squeezing the spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 10:00 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Nazma Bepari, 59, female. Mrs. Bepari reports producing more sputum than usual and has a long history of smoking. She states that her breathing symptoms flared up after rubbish was burned near her home in Bashundhara. She works as an architect and has no significant past medical history. She denies chest pain or fever. On examination: SpO2 86%, BP 124/79 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 77 kg. Auscultation reveals widespread wheezing and reduced breath sounds bilaterally. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Tania Molla, 31, female. Mrs. Molla attends for review regarding itchy raised welts that come and go, symptoms that started after a new food or medicine, and intermittent swelling of her lips. She notes these outbreaks started after eating hilsa at a family dinner in Kushtia. She works as a call centre agent and has no chronic illnesses. She denies any breathing difficulty. On examination: about 25 welts on the trunk and arms, BP 135/84 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 72 kg. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid the suspected food, keep a symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if the tongue or throat swells. Follow-up in 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Ashraf Hasan, 68, male. Mr. Hasan describes symptoms that are worse at night along with numbness in his toes. He mentions these problems started after years of high blood sugar were found at a health camp in Rangpur. He works as a tailor and has no other major diagnosed illnesses. He denies any recent foot injuries. On examination: reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 110/71 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 93 kg. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Mahfuz Awal, 78, male. Mr. Awal reports gritty burning eyes and long hours of screen time. He notes his discomfort began after long gaming sessions at home in Motijheel. He works as a homemaker and has no chronic medical conditions. He denies any sudden loss of vision. On examination: tear break-up time 7 seconds, BP 112/82 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 43 kg. Interestingly, he presents with eyes that water all day rather than feeling dry. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Laila Sultana, 58, female. Mrs. Sultana complains of long hours of screen time, gritty burning eyes, and symptoms that are notably worse in air conditioning. She mentions her issues have been worse since starting night shifts at a call centre in Rajshahi. She works as a sales representative and has no known systemic comorbidities. She denies eye discharge or pain. On examination: tear break-up time 6 seconds, BP 130/82 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 55 kg. Conjunctiva is clear without acute infection. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Shampa Paul, 31, female. Mrs. Paul attends for review complaining of itching, thick white discharge, and soreness. She notes these symptoms started after a course of antibiotics taken in Gazipur. She works as a garment factory worker and has no underlying chronic illnesses. She denies pelvic pain or fever. On examination: random blood glucose 5.8 mmol/L, BP 124/70 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 45 kg. Speculum examination reveals cottage-cheese-like discharge with mucosal erythema. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 12:00 PM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Sabina Alam, 27, female. Miss Alam presents with weight gain, feeling slow and tired, and dry skin. She noticed these changes when a cold winter in Rampura felt much harder than usual. She works as an NGO field officer and has no prior medical history. She denies any heat intolerance or palpitations. On examination: TSH 10.2 mIU/L, BP 120/84 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 74 kg. Skin is dry and reflexes show delayed relaxation. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 12:30 PM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Kamal Alam, 54, male. Mr. Alam returns for a follow-up review for being unable to raise his arm and a stiff shoulder for weeks. He explains this started after weeks of keeping the arm still following a sprain in Mirpur. He works as a software developer and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies acute trauma or redness over the joint. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 110 degrees, BP 131/80 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 71 kg. Passive range of motion is restricted in all planes. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 12:30 PM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Ehsan Hossain, 25, male. Mr. Hossain presents with thick nasal discharge for over ten days, a blocked nose, and pressure over his cheeks and forehead. He states his illness started after a dusty journey to Kushtia. He works as a nurse and has no comorbid conditions. He denies any visual changes. On examination: temperature 100.4°F, BP 113/70 mmHg, pulse 105 bpm, weight 76 kg. Tenderness is noted over the maxillary sinuses. Assessment: Acute sinusitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use steam inhalation twice daily and drink warm fluids. Follow-up in 10 days.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 03:00 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Zakia Miah, 64, female. Mrs. Miah reports having a fever and cough with yellow or green sputum. She notes her illness began after caring for a sick relative in Kamrangirchar. She works as a madrasa teacher and has no chronic medical history. She denies chest pain. On examination: temperature 103.5°F, BP 130/83 mmHg, pulse 95 bpm, SpO2 91%, weight 56 kg. Chest auscultation reveals bronchial breathing and crackles in the right lower lung zone. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 03:00 PM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Shathi Khan, 31, female. Mrs. Khan complains of an itch that is worse in humid weather, a rash with spreading edges, and a ring-shaped itchy red rash. She states it started after playing football on wet fields in Badda. She works as a shopkeeper and has no other health issues. She denies blistering. On examination: affected area about 4 cm across, BP 110/72 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 79 kg. Annular erythematous plaque with active raised borders and central clearing is visible. Assessment: Tinea corporis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep the skin dry, not share towels, and wash clothes in hot water. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-03-06 02:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tuhin Alam, 50, male. Mr. Alam returns for follow-up regarding belly cramps, loose watery stools, and vomiting. He states these symptoms began after a picnic in Noakhali. He works as a security guard and has Essential hypertension. He denies passing blood in his stool. On examination: pulse 101 bpm, BP 152/96 mmHg, weight 73 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild generalized tenderness. Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink small sips of fluid often, eat rice, bananas, and toast, and wash hands before eating. Follow-up in 2 days if the stools do not settle.

Visit note | 2025-03-06 02:30 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Tahsin Sikder, 51, female. Mrs. Sikder comes in for her first visit reporting that she has been passing urine often and has noticed cuts that heal slowly over recent weeks. She mentions these complaints were found during a routine test before a trip to Lalbagh. She works as a mobile phone repair technician, leads a largely sedentary daily routine, and lives with her family in a busy neighbourhood. She reports no prior formal diagnosis of diabetes, though her mother had high blood sugar in her later years. She denies blurred vision, tingling in her feet, chest pain, or shortness of breath. On general review, she reports feeling tired by late afternoon but sleeps reasonably well at night. On examination: fasting glucose 10.1 mmol/L, BP 121/75 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 92 kg. Heart sounds are normal, chest is clear to auscultation, and abdomen is soft and non-tender. Peripheral pulses are intact, and there are no active foot ulcers. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued today. She was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly for 30 minutes five days a week, check her fasting blood sugar twice weekly, and inspect her feet daily for any injury. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat HbA1c test.

Visit note | 2025-03-06 03:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Lipi Pramanik, 20, female. Miss Pramanik presents with a blocked ear after a cold, mild fever, and muffled hearing. She states her illness began after a cold during a trip to Uttara. She works as a bank officer and has no comorbid conditions. She denies ear discharge or severe vertigo. On examination: temperature 101.3°F, BP 112/70 mmHg, pulse 102 bpm, weight 86 kg. Otoscopy shows an erythematous and bulging tympanic membrane. Assessment: Acute otitis media. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep the ear dry and not insert cotton buds. Follow-up in 1 week.
